summary: Every element appears twice except one; find the one that appears once in O(n) time and O(1) space.
mainInsight: XOR is commutative and associative with x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, so XOR-ing the whole array cancels every pair and leaves the single element.

promptVariants: Why does XOR-ing all numbers leave only the single one, regardless of order?
Why do the pairs cancel under XOR even when they are not adjacent?
cards.answer: XOR is commutative and associative, so duplicates can be brought together: (A^A) ^ (C^C) ^ B = 0 ^ 0 ^ B = B.
cards.explanation: That is exactly the derivation in your docstring.
